recipes.title: The Classic Crunchy Coated Spiced Nuts
recipes.description: The method used for holiday market nuts with a crackly, crunchy shell.
ingredients: 1 lb raw pecan halves or whole almonds
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°F (120°C) and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk egg white and water together until light and foamy.
Add nuts to the egg white mixture and toss until thoroughly coated.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together sugar, cinnamon, and salt.
Pour sugar mixture over coated nuts and toss vigorously until sugar coats every nut evenly.
Spread nuts in a single layer across prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring thoroughly every 15 minutes to prevent burning.
Cool completely on baking sheet before serving or storing.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store in an airtight glass jar or tin at room temperature for up to 3 weeks.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper for a subtle sweet-and-spicy kick.

recipes.title: Spicy Sweet Party Pecans
recipes.description: Bold party nuts with a sweet maple cayenne glaze.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C) and line baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk maple syrup, brown sugar, cayenne, paprika, and salt in a bowl.
Add pecans and toss to coat evenly.
Spread on baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once halfway through.
Cool completely on parchment to allow glaze to set crisp.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Keep in a cool, dry place in a sealed container.
recipes.modifications: Replace cayenne with black pepper for milder warmth.

recipes.title: Sweet & Savory Rosemary Roasted Almonds
recipes.description: Fragrant roasted almonds tossed with fresh rosemary, sea salt, and honey.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Toss almonds with olive oil and honey until coated.
Spread on baking sheet and roast for 15 minutes, stirring once.
Remove from oven, immediately toss with fresh rosemary and sea salt.
Cool completely before serving.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Best enjoyed within 2 weeks of roasting.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/2 tsp black pepper for extra savory depth.

recipes.title: Mom's Soft & Chewy Molasses Spice Cookies
recipes.description: Deeply spiced, crinkly molasses cookies with rich dark brown sugar.
instructions: Whisk flour, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, and salt together in a bowl.
In a stand mixer, beat softened butter and brown sugar until fluffy (approx. 2 mins).
Beat in egg and molasses until smooth.
Gradually add dry ingredients on low speed until dough forms.
Chill dough in refrigerator for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Roll dough into 1-inch balls and roll generously in granulated sugar.
Place 2 inches apart on baking sheets.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes until edges are set and tops are crinkled. Cool 5 mins on pan.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store in an airtight container with a slice of bread to keep soft for weeks.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/2 cup finely chopped candied ginger for extra zing.

recipes.title: Classic Melt-in-Your-Mouth Butter Shortbread
recipes.description: Traditional 3-ingredient Scottish butter shortbread fingers.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Beat softened butter and powdered sugar until creamy.
Add vanilla and salt, then gradually mix in flour until soft dough forms.
Press dough evenly into an 8x8 inch baking dish.
Prick all over with a fork and score into rectangular fingers.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until pale golden.
Cut along score lines while warm, then cool completely in pan.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store in a cookie tin at room temperature.
recipes.modifications: Dip half of each cooled finger in melted dark chocolate.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Sugar Snickerdoodles
recipes.description: Classic pillow-soft snickerdoodles with a crackly cinnamon-sugar crust.
ingredients: 3 tbsp granulated sugar + 1 tbsp cinnamon (for rolling)
instructions: Whisk flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and salt.
Beat butter and 1 1/2 cups sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each.
Mix in dry ingredients until combined.
Roll dough into 1.25-inch balls and roll in cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Place 2 inches apart on parchment-lined baking sheets.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 8 to 10 minutes. Do not overbake!
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store in an airtight container for up to 7 days.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/2 tsp nutmeg to the cinnamon sugar coating.

recipes.title: Classic Rich Chocolate Fudge
recipes.description: Smooth, decadent homemade chocolate fudge topped with flaky sea salt.
instructions: Line an 8x8 inch pan with parchment paper, leaving overhang edges.
In a saucepan over medium-low heat, combine chocolate chips, condensed milk, and butter.
Stir constantly until completely melted and smooth.
Remove from heat, stir in vanilla and salt.
Pour into prepared pan and smooth top with spatula.
Sprinkle with flaky sea salt if desired.
Refrigerate for 2 hours until firm, then cut into square pieces.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks.
recipes.modifications: Fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts or pecans before pouring into pan.

recipes.title: Mom's Pink Peppermint Bark
recipes.description: Mom's classic holiday almond bark infused with peppermint oil, a touch of red oil-based food coloring for a pretty pink hue, and crushed candy canes.
ingredients: 1 to 2 drops red oil-based food coloring
instructions: Melt white almond bark in a heavy saucepan over low heat (or in a microwave-safe bowl in 30-second bursts), stirring until smooth.
Stir in peppermint oil and 1 to 2 drops of red food coloring until the melted bark turns a lovely soft pink color.
Fold in most of the crushed candy canes, reserving a handful for the top.
Pour mixture onto a parchment-lined baking sheet and spread evenly.
Sprinkle reserved crushed candy canes on top.
Set baking sheet outside in the cold garage (or in the fridge) until set and firm, then break into rustic pieces.
recipes.handlingInstructions:
⚠️ SEIZING HAZARD WARNING: NEVER use water-based liquid food coloring or water-based extracts in melted almond bark or chocolate! Even a single drop of water will cause the melted bark to instantly SEIZE into a stiff, grainy, clumping paste and ruin the entire batch! You MUST use oil-based food coloring (or gel/powder) and oil-based peppermint oil or candy oil flavoring.

Mom's Secret: Always use real candy canes—starlight mints do not have the same classic holiday flavor! Set outside in the cold garage to cool.
recipes.modifications: Layer over dark chocolate for Dark Chocolate Peppermint Bark.
recipes.memories:
Mom's pink peppermint bark was always a weakness of mine.

As a kid, I always knew what she was making when she'd pull out that double boiler and start whacking candy canes in a Ziploc bag with her rolling pin. It wasn't a big recipe, but sometimes she'd let me whack the candy canes a few times myself. It always seemed to take forever for those huge chunks of almond bark to melt. Then she'd add a few drops of peppermint and a little food coloring, and it would be ready for the candy canes.

She'd let me pour them in, and she'd stir like crazy as she pulled it from the heat. She already had the cookie sheet and parchment paper ready. That ooey-gooey pink mixture would slowly pour out of the pan.

Like her peanut brittle, it would go out on the car, sitting on a towel to cool. She would spend two full days in the kitchen making sweet treats for the holiday season, and Dad and I were the lucky ones who got to reap the rewards.

Dad knew it, too. Throughout the season, he would often sneak in for a sweet treat. The fridge was packed full of bags and Tupperware containers filled with all kinds of goodies.

Looking back, some of my best memories are from the time I got to spend with my mom in that kitchen.

recipes.title: Mom's Salted Caramels
recipes.description: Chewy, buttery homemade caramels sprinkled with coarse sea salt and individually wrapped in wax paper.
instructions: Line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper and grease lightly.
In a heavy 3-quart saucepan, combine sugar, corn syrup, heavy cream, and butter over medium heat.
Stir constantly until sugar dissolves and butter melts.
Attach a candy thermometer and cook, stirring frequently, until mixture reaches 248°F (firm-ball stage).
Remove from heat immediately and stir in vanilla extract.
Pour into prepared baking pan and let cool for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle flaky sea salt evenly across the top.
Let cool completely (approx. 2 hours), then cut into squares and wrap in wax paper.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Wrap individually in wax paper to prevent sticking. Store in a cool place for up to 3 weeks.
recipes.modifications: Dip half of each caramel in melted dark chocolate.

recipes.title: Classic Chewy Pecan Pralines
recipes.description: Authentic Southern brown sugar pecan pralines.
instructions: Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a heavy saucepan, combine sugars, heavy cream, milk, and butter.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Bring to a boil until candy thermometer reaches 238°F (soft-ball stage).
Remove from heat, stir in pecans and vanilla.
Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon for 2-3 minutes until mixture thickens and loses shine.
Quickly drop by spoonfuls onto parchment paper.
Allow pralines to cool and harden completely.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store individually wrapped or layered with wax paper in airtight tin.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/4 tsp cinnamon for warm spiced flavor.

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Peanut Butter Fudge
recipes.description: Creamy, melt-in-your-mouth homemade peanut butter fudge.
instructions: Butter an 8x8 inch baking dish.
In a saucepan, combine sugar and milk, bringing to a rolling boil.
Boil for 2.5 minutes while stirring.
Remove from heat and immediately stir in butter, peanut butter, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into the prepared dish and let cool until set.
Cut into squares.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Do not over-boil or the fudge will become grainy. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.
recipes.modifications: Swirl with chocolate fudge for a classic combo.

recipes.title: Banana Nut Bread
recipes.description: Moist, delicious banana bread loaded with nuts and cozy spices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 4x8 inch loaf pan.
In a mixing bowl, mash the ripe bananas with a fork.
Stir in melted butter, sugar, egg, and vanilla.
Mix in baking soda and salt.
Add flour last, mixing just until incorporated. Fold in nuts.
Pour into loaf pan and bake for 50-60 minutes.
Cool before slicing.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Wrap tightly in plastic wrap or foil. Banana bread tastes even better and gets extra moist on day two!
recipes.modifications: Add 1/2 cup chocolate chips or cranberries.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Bread
recipes.description: Spiced autumn pumpkin bread that is moist and flavorful.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a loaf pan.
Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a bowl.
In another bowl, mix pumpkin puree, oil, sugar, and eggs until smooth.
Combine wet and dry ingredients just until blended.
Pour into loaf pan and bake for 50-55 minutes.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes before removing.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store wrapped at room temperature for up to 4 days.
recipes.modifications: Top with pepitas (pumpkin seeds) before baking.

recipes.title: Classic Brownies
recipes.description: Rich, chewy chocolate brownies with a crackly top.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease an 8x8 inch baking dish.
In a bowl, mix melted butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla.
Whisk in cocoa powder, flour, salt, and baking powder until smooth.
Spread into baking dish and bake for 25-30 minutes.
Cool before cutting into squares.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/2 cup chopped walnuts or chocolate chips.

recipes.title: Lemon Bars
recipes.description: Tart, sweet lemon filling on a buttery shortbread crust.
ingredients: Crust: 1 cup flour, 1/4 cup powdered sugar, 1/2 cup butter, softened
Filling: 1 cup sugar, 2 tbsp flour, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 2 eggs, 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tbsp lemon zest
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Combine crust ingredients and press into an 8x8 inch pan. Bake for 15 minutes.
Whisk filling ingredients together until smooth and pour over hot crust.
Bake for an additional 20 minutes until set.
Cool completely and dust with powdered sugar before cutting.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate for clean cuts. Best served chilled.
recipes.modifications: Dust with extra powdered sugar right before serving.

recipes.title: Festive Cranberry Orange Bread
recipes.description: Zesty orange loaf dotted with tart fresh cranberries.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease loaf pan.
Mix dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Whisk egg, orange zest, orange juice, and oil in a small bowl.
Combine wet and dry, then fold in cranberries.
Bake for 50 minutes until golden.
Cool on wire rack.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store wrapped in foil to keep moist.
recipes.modifications: Drizzle with orange glaze.

recipes.title: Soft Sugar Cookies
recipes.description: Pillow-soft sugar cookies perfect for holiday decorating.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix flour, baking soda, and baking powder.
Cream butter and sugar until smooth. Beat in egg and vanilla.
Gradually blend in dry ingredients.
Roll into 1-inch balls, place on baking sheet, and flatten slightly.
Bake for 8-10 minutes. Cool on wire rack.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Decorate with buttercream frosting once cooled.
recipes.modifications: Roll in colored sanding sugar before baking.

recipes.title: Mom's Best Classic Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: Golden, buttery chocolate chip cookies with crisp edges and soft chewy centers.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in small bowl.
Beat butter, granulated sugar, dark brown sugar, and vanilla in large mixer bowl until creamy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Gradually beat in flour mixture.
Stir in chocolate morsels and nuts.
Drop by rounded tablespoon onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake for 9 to 11 minutes until golden brown. Cool on baking sheets for 2 minutes.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Store in an airtight container with a slice of bread to keep soft.
recipes.modifications: Use half semi-sweet and half dark chocolate chunks for extra cocoa flavor.
recipes.memories: Mom's warm chocolate chip cookies straight out of the oven were the legendary after-school treat. The whole kitchen would smell like sweet butter and toasted chocolate!

recipes.title: Vanilla Cupcakes
recipes.description: Fluffy, tender vanilla cupcakes made from scratch.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and line muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cream butter and sugar. Add eggs one at a time, then vanilla.
Alternate adding dry ingredients and milk until smooth.
Fill liners 2/3 full and bake for 18-20 minutes.
Cool before frosting.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Frost with vanilla or chocolate buttercream.
recipes.modifications: Add rainbow sprinkles to batter for funfetti cupcakes.

recipes.title: Classic Fluffy Vanilla Buttercream
recipes.description: Whipped, bakery-style vanilla buttercream frosting.
instructions: Beat softened butter in stand mixer for 3 full minutes until pale and creamy.
Gradually add powdered sugar 1 cup at a time on low speed.
Add heavy cream, vanilla, and salt.
Whip on high speed for 3 minutes until light, fluffy, and spreadable.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate in airtight container up to 2 weeks.
recipes.modifications: Add 2 tbsp cocoa powder for chocolate buttercream.

recipes.title: Rich Cream Cheese Frosting
recipes.description: Tangy cream cheese frosting perfect for pumpkin bread and gingerbread.
instructions: Beat cream cheese and butter together until smooth and free of lumps.
Add vanilla and salt.
Gradually beat in powdered sugar until creamy and smooth.
Chill 15 minutes before piping or spreading.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Keep refrigerated; bring to room temp 10 mins before piping.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/2 tsp cinnamon for spiced cream cheese frosting.

recipes.title: Mom's Savory Glazed Meatloaf
recipes.description: Classic comforting beef meatloaf topped with a sweet and tangy ketchup glaze.
ingredients: 1 cup Ritz cracker crumbs or breadcrumbs
Glaze: 1/2 cup ketchup, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp yellow mustard
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil.
Soak cracker crumbs in milk in a large bowl for 5 minutes.
Add ground beef, diced onion, eggs, garlic, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper. Mix gently with hands until combined (do not overwork).
Shape meat mixture into a 9x5 inch loaf on prepared baking sheet.
Whisk glaze ingredients together in a small bowl and brush half over top of meatloaf.
Bake for 45 minutes, brush remaining glaze over top, and bake another 15 minutes until internal temp reaches 160°F.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; great for cold meatloaf sandwiches!
recipes.modifications: Top with 3 slices of uncooked bacon before applying glaze.

recipes.title: Mom's Best Classic Peanut Brittle
recipes.description: Crisp, airy homemade peanut brittle made with raw peanuts, butter, and baking soda.
instructions: Butter two large rimmed baking sheets generously.
In a heavy 3-quart saucepan, combine sugar, corn syrup, and water over medium heat.
Stir until sugar dissolves and mixture comes to a boil.
Stir in butter and raw peanuts. Attach candy thermometer.
Cook, stirring frequently, until thermometer reaches 300°F (hard-crack stage).
Remove from heat immediately; stir in baking soda, vanilla, and salt (mixture will foam up).
Quickly pour and spread mixture thinly onto prepared baking sheets.
Set baking sheet outside in the cold garage (or in fridge) until set and firm, then break into pieces.
recipes.handlingInstructions: ⚠️ SEIZING HAZARD WARNING: NEVER use water-based liquid food coloring or water near hot sugar candy. Store brittle in an airtight container with wax paper between layers.
recipes.modifications: Substitute raw pecans or cashews for peanuts.
recipes.memories: Mom made batches of this brittle every Christmas. She would set the pans outside in the cold garage to set quickly, and the peanut brittle always turned out wonderfully light and crackly!

recipes.title: Classic Original Chex Mix
recipes.description: The timeless crispy party snack baked with seasoned butter glaze.
ingredients: 1 cup garlic-flavored bagel chips or rye chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°F (120°C).
In a large bowl, combine Corn Chex, Rice Chex, Wheat Chex, mixed nuts, pretzels, and bagel chips.
In a small bowl, whisk together melted butter, Worcestershire sauce, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Pour butter mixture evenly over cereal mixture; stir until thoroughly and evenly coated.
Spread mixture evenly across two large rimmed baking sheets.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring thoroughly every 15 minutes.
Spread onto paper towels or parchment to cool completely before serving.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Stirring every 15 minutes during baking is essential for an evenly crisp, toasted crunch! Store in an airtight container for up to 4 weeks.
recipes.modifications: Add cheese crackers (like Cheez-Its) or a dash of hot sauce to the butter glaze for extra zesty flavor.

recipes.title: Mom's Creamy Baked Macaroni & Cheese
recipes.description: Rich, velvety baked macaroni and cheese made with sharp cheddar, butter, and a golden toasted breadcrumb crust.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Gruyère or Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
1/2 cup panko or Ritz cracker crumbs
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Cook elbow macaroni in salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than package directions; drain.
Melt 1/4 cup butter in a saucepan over medium heat; whisk in flour and cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk, salt, and pepper; cook until smooth and thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in shredded cheddar and Gruyère until completely melted.
Fold in cooked macaroni and pour into prepared baking dish.
Toss crumbs with 2 tbsp melted butter and sprinkle over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and golden brown on top.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Shred cheese from the block! Pre-shredded bagged cheese contains anti-caking agents that prevent a silky smooth melt.
recipes.modifications: Add cooked crumbled bacon or diced ham for a savory twist.
recipes.memories: Mom always baked this side dish for holiday family dinners alongside her savory meatloaf or roast turkey. The crispy golden breadcrumbs on top were always the best part!

recipes.title: Mom's Creamy Homemade Hot Chocolate
recipes.description: Rich, velvety stovetop hot chocolate made with real chocolate, whole milk, cocoa, and a hint of vanilla.
ingredients: 1/2 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips or chopped dark chocolate
Mini marshmallows or whipped cream for serving
instructions: In a medium saucepan, whisk together whole milk, cocoa powder, sugar, and salt over medium-low heat until warm (do not boil).
Add chocolate chips and whisk constantly until completely melted, smooth, and creamy.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract.
Ladle into cozy mugs and top with marshmallows, whipped cream, or a dash of cinnamon.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Never let the milk boil! Slow medium-low heat keeps the chocolate smooth and prevents scalding.
recipes.modifications: Add a pinch of cinnamon or a splash of peppermint extract for a festive holiday twist.
recipes.memories: On snowy winter afternoons, Mom always had a warm pot of homemade hot chocolate ready when we came inside after playing in the snow. Topping it with extra marshmallows was mandatory!

recipes.title: Traditional Herb Butter Roast Turkey
recipes.description: Classic whole oven-roasted turkey seasoned with garlic herb butter, aromatic root vegetables, and a crisp golden skin.
ingredients: 1 (12 to 14 lb) whole fresh turkey, giblets and neck removed
2 cups low-sodium chicken or turkey broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C) and position rack in lower third of oven.
Pat turkey completely dry inside and out with paper towels.
In a bowl, mix softened butter, rosemary, thyme, sage, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Gently loosen skin over turkey breast and rub half the herb butter directly onto the meat under the skin.
Rub remaining herb butter all over the outside skin.
Stuff turkey cavity with quartered onion, lemon, and extra herbs.
Place chopped carrots and celery in roasting pan and rest turkey breast-side up on roasting rack over veggies; pour broth into bottom of pan.
Roast 3 to 3.5 hours, basting with pan juices every 45 minutes, until a meat thermometer inserted into thickest part of breast/thigh reaches 155°F (68°C).
Transfer turkey to carving board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 20 to 30 minutes. Carryover heat will gently raise internal temperature to 165°F (74°C) while locking in all natural juices!
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip (155°F Carryover Cooking Secret): Pull turkey out of oven at 155°F! Carryover heat during the 20-minute rest will coast the temperature up to the target 165°F, keeping meat ultra-moist instead of overcooking to 175°F+.
recipes.modifications: Dry brine 24 hours ahead for extra crispy skin and deeply seasoned, tender meat.

recipes.title: Crispy Spatchcock Roast Turkey
recipes.description: Flattened, butterflied roast turkey cooked at high heat for extra crispy skin and juicy, evenly-cooked meat in half the time.
ingredients: 1 (12 to 14 lb) whole fresh turkey, thawed
1/4 cup butter, softened (for under the skin)
2 to 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (for lubricating the outside skin)
1/2 cup chopped carrots (placed in pan bottom under bird)
2 to 3 cloves garlic, minced (placed in pan bottom under bird)
1 tbsp fresh chopped thyme and rosemary
instructions: Dry Brine (24 Hours Ahead): 24 hours before cooking, coat turkey inside and out with coarse kosher salt and chill uncovered in fridge to dry the skin and season meat throughout.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a roasting pan with foil, and add 1/2 cup chopped carrots and 2-3 minced garlic cloves to the bottom of the pan.
Spatchcock Turkey: Place turkey breast-side down on a large cutting board. Using heavy-duty poultry shears, cut along both sides of the backbone to remove it completely.
Flip turkey breast-side up. Press down firmly on the center breastbone with the palms of your hands until you hear a crack and turkey lies flat.
Pat turkey skin thoroughly dry inside and out with paper towels.
Gently loosen the skin over the breast and thighs with your fingers. Rub softened butter directly onto the meat under the skin.
Coat the outside skin generously with olive oil until thoroughly lubricated.
Sprinkle salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and chopped herbs all over the oiled outside skin so the spices cling evenly.
Place flattened turkey on roasting rack over the carrots and minced garlic. Roast at 425°F for 70 to 80 minutes until breast reaches 155°F (68°C).

Rest 20 minutes before carving. Carryover heat will gently raise internal temperature to the ideal 165°F target while keeping meat ultra-juicy! Use pan drippings with roasted carrots and garlic to make gravy.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip (155°F Pull Temp): Pull at 155°F and rest 20 mins to reach 165°F carryover temp. Dry brining 24 hours ahead + butter under skin + olive oil on top produces the ultimate juicy, crackling-crispy turkey!
recipes.modifications: Spatchcocking cooks the turkey in half the time and produces ultra-crispy skin across the entire bird!

recipes.title: Southern Candied Yams
recipes.description: Tender sweet potato slices baked in a rich, caramelized glaze of brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla.
ingredients: 4 large sweet potatoes or yams, peeled and sliced into 1/2-inch rounds
1 cup mini marshmallows or pecan halves (optional topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Arrange sliced sweet potatoes in an even layer in the prepared baking dish.
In a saucepan over medium heat, melt butter with brown sugar, maple syrup, cinnamon, nutmeg, vanilla, and salt, stirring until sugar is completely dissolved into a thick glaze.
Pour warm brown sugar glaze evenly over the sweet potatoes.
Cover baking dish tightly with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove foil, spoon glaze from bottom of dish back over potatoes, and bake uncovered for another 15 minutes until potatoes are tender and sauce is thick and bubbling.
Optional: Top with mini marshmallows or pecans and broil for 2–3 minutes until toasted and golden.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat gently in oven or microwave.
recipes.modifications: Top with toasted pecans for a nutty crunch or a splash of orange juice in the glaze for bright citrus flavor.
recipes.memories: No holiday family dinner was complete without a piping hot dish of sweet, caramelized candied yams right next to the roast turkey!

recipes.title: Classic Green Bean Casserole
recipes.description: Tender green beans folded into a creamy mushroom sauce and baked until bubbling, topped with crunchy French fried onions.
ingredients: 4 cups cooked green beans (trimmed fresh or frozen, drained)
1 (10.5 oz) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1/2 cup whole milk or heavy cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 1.5-quart baking dish.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together cream of mushroom soup, milk, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, and black pepper until smooth.
Fold in green beans and 2/3 cup of French fried onions (plus optional cheddar cheese).
Pour green bean mixture into prepared baking dish and spread evenly.
Bake uncovered for 25 minutes until hot and bubbling around edges.
Remove from oven, stir gently, and sprinkle remaining 2/3 cup French fried onions across the top.
Bake for an additional 5 minutes until onions are golden brown and crunchy.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days.
recipes.modifications: Add sautéed sliced mushrooms or crispy bacon bits for extra savory depth.
recipes.memories: That irresistible golden crunch of fried onions on top of rich, creamy green beans is a timeless holiday tradition!

recipes.title: Divine Mashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Ultra-creamy, fluffy mashed potatoes whipped with rich butter, sour cream, garlic, and heavy cream.
ingredients: 3 lbs Yukon Gold or Russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 cup heavy cream or whole milk, warm
1 tsp salt (plus 1 tbsp for boiling water)
2 tbsp fresh chopped chives or green onions (garnish)
instructions: Place cubed potatoes in a large stockpot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and add 1 tbsp salt.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-high and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
Drain potatoes thoroughly in a colander and return to the warm pot for 1 minute to let residual steam evaporate.
Mash potatoes with a potato masher or ricer until smooth.
Add softened butter, sour cream, warm heavy cream, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Whip gently with a wooden spoon or hand mixer until velvety smooth and fluffy.
Garnish with fresh chopped chives and an extra pat of butter before serving warm.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Yukon Gold potatoes yield the creamiest texture! Never over-whip or use a food processor, which causes gummy potatoes.
recipes.modifications: Fold in 1/2 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese or crispy bacon bits for loaded mashed potatoes.
recipes.memories: These divine, velvety mashed potatoes are the ultimate holiday crowd-pleaser—rich, buttery, and perfect for soaking up roast turkey gravy!

recipes.title: Classic Brown Sugar Pineapple Baked Ham
recipes.description: Showstopping spiral-sliced bone-in city ham studded with clove-pinned pineapple rings and cherries, glazed in brown sugar, maple syrup, and Dijon mustard.
ingredients: 1 (8 to 10 lb) pre-cooked spiral sliced or bone-in city ham
1 (20 oz) can pineapple slices in juice (reserve juice)
1/4 cup pure maple syrup or honey
1/2 cup apple cider or dry white wine (for pan bottom)
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C) and position rack in lower third of oven.
Place ham cut-side down in a roasting pan. Pour reserved pineapple juice and 1/2 cup apple cider (or white wine) into the bottom of the pan.
Cover pan tightly with aluminum foil to lock in moisture and bake for 1.5 hours (approx. 10-12 minutes per pound).
In a saucepan over medium heat, whisk brown sugar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, and cinnamon until sugar dissolves into a warm caramel glaze.
Remove ham from oven and discard foil. Score diamond patterns if un-sliced.
Attach pineapple slices and maraschino cherries to the ham using toothpicks. Insert whole cloves in center diamond intersections.
Brush half the warm brown sugar glaze generously all over the ham and fruit.

Return uncovered ham to oven and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 to 30 minutes, basting with remaining glaze every 10 minutes, until glaze is bubbling and caramelized and internal temp reaches 140°F (60°C).
Transfer to carving board, spoon pan juices over top, and rest 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Low and slow reheating covered at 325°F keeps ham juicy! Apply the brown sugar glaze in the last 25 minutes uncovered so sugars caramelize without burning.
recipes.modifications: Add 2 tbsp Bourbon or Dark Rum to the glaze for rich caramel oak notes!

recipes.title: Easy Honey Glazed Boneless Ham
recipes.description: Effortless, easy-to-slice boneless ham baked with a sweet, sticky cinnamon honey mustard glaze.
ingredients: 1 (4 to 6 lb) pre-cooked boneless or formed ham
2 tbsp whole grain or Dijon mustard
1/2 cup apple juice or Riesling white wine (for pan bottom)
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C) and line baking pan with foil.
Place boneless ham flat-side down on baking rack in pan. Pour apple juice or white wine into pan bottom.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 1 hour (approx. 12-15 minutes per pound).
In a small bowl, whisk honey, brown sugar, mustard, melted butter, and cinnamon until smooth.
Remove foil, brush half the honey glaze over ham, and bake uncovered at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes.
Brush with remaining glaze and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until top is bubbly, sticky, and caramelized (140°F internal temp).
Rest 10 minutes before effortless slicing.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate leftover ham in airtight containers for 3 to 4 days. Save ham slice trimmings for morning omelets or split pea soup!
recipes.modifications: Substitute maple syrup for honey for a rich autumn maple glaze.

recipes.title: Mom's Classic Baked Scalloped Corn
recipes.description: Comforting holiday corn casserole baked with sweet corn, creamed corn, butter, Ritz cracker crumbs, and a golden bubbly top.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can whole kernel sweet corn, drained
1 cup crushed Ritz crackers (approx. 1 sleeve), divided
1/2 cup whole milk or heavy cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a 2-quart baking dish.
In a large bowl, whisk together beaten eggs, melted butter, milk, sugar, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Stir in whole kernel corn, cream-style corn, and 3/4 cup of crushed Ritz crackers (and optional cheddar cheese).
Pour corn mixture into prepared baking dish and smooth the top.
Sprinkle remaining 1/4 cup crushed Ritz crackers over the top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until set in the center and golden brown and bubbling around the edges.
Rest 10 minutes before serving warm.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days. Reheat in oven or microwave.
recipes.modifications: Add 1/4 cup diced bell pepper or pimientos for a festive splash of red and green color!
recipes.memories: Mom's baked scalloped corn was a constant star on our holiday table. The sweet creamed corn mixed with buttery Ritz crackers made it everyone's favorite side dish!

recipes.title: Greg's Skillet Scalloped Corn
recipes.description: Fast, 15-minute stovetop skillet scalloped corn seared in sweet butter with crushed crackers—saves oven space on holidays and makes an easy year-round side dish!
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans whole kernel sweet corn, drained (or 3 cups fresh/frozen corn)
1 cup crushed Ritz crackers or saltine crackers
1/2 cup heavy cream or whole milk
2 tbsp chopped fresh chives or parsley (garnish)
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet (cast iron or heavy skillet) over medium heat.
Add crushed crackers to the hot melted butter and stir for 2 minutes until light golden and fragrant.
Add drained sweet corn, heavy cream, sugar, salt, and black pepper to the skillet.
Stir continuously and simmer over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until cream thickens and coats the corn in a rich, buttery sauce.
Garnish with fresh chives and serve piping hot straight from the skillet!
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Making scalloped corn in a skillet on the stovetop frees up valuable oven space during busy Thanksgiving dinners, and takes under 15 minutes for any weeknight meal!
recipes.modifications: Stir in 1/2 cup shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese in the last minute for cheesy skillet corn.
recipes.memories: Greg's quick skillet method is a lifesaver when the holiday oven is packed full with turkey and ham. It delivers all the rich, buttery cracker goodness of baked scalloped corn in a fraction of the time!

recipes.title: Traditional Pumpkin Pie
recipes.description: The classic, velvet-smooth holiday pumpkin pie baked in a flaky crust with warm cinnamon, ginger, cloves, and evaporated milk.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can pumpkin puree (100% pure pumpkin)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a small bowl, whisk together sugar, salt, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs. Stir in pumpkin puree and the sugar-spice mixture until smooth.
Gradually stir in evaporated milk until thoroughly combined into a smooth liquid filling.
Pour filling into the unbaked deep-dish pie crust.
Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350°F (175°C) and bake for an additional 40 to 50 minutes until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack for 2 hours. Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve with a generous dollop of whipped cream.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: High-heat baking at 425°F for the first 15 minutes sets the pie crust, while lowering to 350°F bakes the custard filling until silky smooth without cracking!
recipes.modifications: Substitute 1 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice for the cinnamon, ginger, and cloves.
recipes.memories: The scent of warm pumpkin, cinnamon, and cloves baking on Thanksgiving morning is the purest scent of home and holiday family traditions!

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Peanut Butter Pie
recipes.description: Rich, velvety no-bake peanut butter pie whipped with cream cheese and fluffy topping, set in a crunchy graham cracker crust and topped with hot fudge drizzle and chopped peanuts.
ingredients: 1 (9-inch) graham cracker or chocolate Oreo pie crust
1 cup creamy peanut butter (Jif or Skippy)
1 (8 oz) tub whipped topping (Cool Whip), thawed, divided
1/4 cup hot fudge sauce or melted dark chocolate (for drizzle)
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, beat softened cream cheese and creamy peanut butter together until light and fluffy.
Gradually add powdered sugar and vanilla extract, beating on low speed until smooth and creamy.
Gently fold in 2 cups (approx. 6 oz) of thawed whipped topping with a spatula until no white streaks remain.
Spoon peanut butter filling into the prepared graham cracker pie crust, smoothing the top with a spatula.
Spread remaining whipped topping over the top of the pie.
Drizzle generously with warm hot fudge sauce and sprinkle chopped salted peanuts over the top.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours (or freeze for 1 hour) until chilled and firm before slicing.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Use regular commercial creamy peanut butter (like Jif or Skippy). Natural oil-separating peanut butter will cause the pie filling to separate!
recipes.modifications: Use an Oreo or Nutter Butter cookie crust for an extra decadent chocolate peanut butter combo!
recipes.memories: The first time I had this pie was down on vacation in the Lake of the Ozarks Bagnell Dam area at the Millstone Lodge when I was about 8 years old. Ever since, I've been obsessed with that pie! Mom made them over the years for special occasions, but that first magical bite in the Ozarks will forever be burned in my memory.

recipes.title: King's Hawaiian Sweet Dinner Rolls
recipes.description: Pillow-soft, golden Hawaiian sweet rolls baked with pineapple juice, honey, butter, and vanilla with a sticky sweet honey-butter glaze.
ingredients: 1 (0.25 oz) packet active dry yeast (2 1/4 tsp)
2 large eggs (1 for dough, 1 for egg wash)
2 tbsp melted butter + 1 tbsp honey (for post-bake glaze)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk warm pineapple juice, warm milk, 1 tbsp sugar, and active dry yeast. Let sit 5 to 10 minutes until foamy.
Whisk in melted butter, remaining sugar, honey, 1 egg, vanilla extract, and salt.
Gradually stir in all-purpose flour until a soft dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 6 to 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a greased bowl, cover with a warm towel, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled in size.
Divide dough into 12 to 15 equal portions, shape into smooth round rolls, and place in a greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Cover and let rise for 30 to 45 minutes until puffy.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Beat remaining egg with 1 tbsp water and brush gently over tops of rolls.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes until deep golden brown on top.
Immediately brush tops with melted butter and honey while piping hot. Cool 10 minutes before pulling apart!
recipes.handlingInstructions: Pro Tip: Warm pineapple juice gives these rolls their iconic tropical sweetness! Never heat juice above 115°F or it will kill the yeast.
recipes.modifications: Slice rolls horizontally to make iconic Hawaiian slider sandwiches with ham, Swiss cheese, and poppyseed butter glaze!
recipes.memories: These irresistibly sweet, cloud-soft Hawaiian rolls are always the first bread to disappear from the Thanksgiving table!

recipes.title: Classic Fluffy Dinner Rolls
recipes.description: Golden, feather-light homemade yeast dinner rolls brushed with salted butter right out of the oven.
instructions: In a stand mixer or large bowl, combine warm milk, melted butter, sugar, egg, and instant yeast.
Add salt and 2 cups of flour; beat on medium speed for 2 minutes.
Gradually add remaining flour until dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide dough into 12 equal balls and place in a greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Cover with a towel and let rise in a warm place for 45 minutes to 1 hour until doubled.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake rolls for 15 to 18 minutes until golden brown on top.
Brush generously with melted salted butter immediately upon pulling from the oven.
recipes.handlingInstructions: Refrigerate leftover rolls wrapped tightly in foil for 3 to 4 days, or freeze baked rolls for up to 3 months. Reheat at 350°F for 5 minutes.
recipes.modifications: Sprinkle with coarse sea salt or garlic butter before serving.
recipes.memories: Golden dinner rolls fresh out of the oven were pure magic. Slathering them with extra butter while piping hot was an absolute holiday ritual!
